## 正文

Hey @kaiyux 👋

truly impressive work. 24 skills covering everything from Nsight profiling to CUDA graph optimization to Triton kernel writing. The depth here is remarkable. You can tell this was built by people who actually debug LLM inference bottlenecks daily.

ran your skills through `tessl skill review` at work and found some targeted improvements for the `ad-model-onboard` skill. Here's full before/after:

| Skill | Before | After | Change |
|-------|--------|-------|--------|
| ad-model-onboard | 68% | 89% | **+21%** |

the other 22 skills in the repo scored between 70%–99%, great quality across the board. I focused on this one because it had the most improvement headroom.

<details>
<summary>What changed</summary>

**Description frontmatter (68% → 100%)**
- Replaced folded scalar (`>`) with a quoted string for standard YAML formatting
- Added an explicit "Use when..." clause with natural trigger terms (`onboard`, `convert`, `port`, `HuggingFace model`, `TensorRT-LLM AutoDeploy`, `custom model onboarding`, `AD custom model`, `prefill-only export`, `model equivalence testing`)
- This helps Claude Code select the right skill when a user asks about model onboarding

**Progressive disclosure (1/3 → 2/3)**
- Extracted the 137-line "Sharding-aware IR model porting" section into `references/sharding-ir.md`
- This covers the step-by-step porting procedure, reference examples, layer-specific sharding patterns, common pitfalls, and validation checklist
- Replaced with a concise 3-line summary + link in the main SKILL.md
- SKILL.md reduced from 494 → 358 lines while preserving all actionable content

</details>

---

quick honest disclosure. I work at https://github.com/tesslio where we build tooling around skills like these. Not a pitch, just saw room for improvement and wanted to contribute.

If you want to self-improve your skills, or define your own scenarios to pressure test, just ask your agent (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) to evaluate and optimize your skill with Tessl. Ping me [@yogesh-tessl](https://github.com/yogesh-tessl), if you hit any snags.
